riskScenarios.title: Supplier-enabled ransomware across production
riskScenarios.statement: A financially motivated actor compromises a managed service provider identity, uses standing privileged access to reach production administration, and encrypts the platforms behind payments, checkout and fulfilment.
consequences: Multi-day loss of payment processing
Fulfilment halted across three distribution centres
Regulatory and acquirer notification

riskScenarios.title: Concentration of business services on one identity platform
riskScenarios.statement: Compromise of the identity platform enables an actor to reach several critical business services at once, because staff, partner and service identities all resolve there.
consequences: Simultaneous loss of several services
No clean administrative path to recover

riskScenarios.title: Unsupported warehouse platform taken out of service
riskScenarios.statement: An actor reaches the legacy data centre through the corporate network and disables the unsupported warehouse platform, stopping despatch with no patch path and an untested restore.
consequences: Despatch stops across three sites
Manual fulfilment at a fraction of throughput

riskScenarios.title: Bulk exposure of customer records
riskScenarios.statement: An actor exploits an internet-facing weakness in the checkout service, inherits over-permissioned workload identity, and extracts customer records in bulk.
consequences: Notification across three regulatory regimes
Loss of customer confidence during launch year

riskScenarios.title: Partner credential abuse reaching internal systems
riskScenarios.statement: Reused partner credentials succeed against the extranet, and because partner identities share the staff directory the actor begins from inside the identity boundary.
consequences: Order and customer data extraction
Partner trust damage

riskScenarios.title: Build pipeline used as a route into production
riskScenarios.statement: An engineer is compromised, the build pipeline's standing production credentials are abused, and the actor is deployed into production by Nexora's own automation.
consequences: Trusted change becomes the attack
Difficult to distinguish malicious from routine deployment

riskScenarios.title: Slow theft of the behavioural data lake
riskScenarios.statement: A patient actor obtains analyst access and extracts commercially sensitive behavioural data over months, below the threshold of any current detection.
consequences: Loss of the commercial differentiator behind Insight Services
Contractual exposure to enterprise clients

riskScenarios.title: Logistics partner compromise stopping fulfilment
riskScenarios.statement: The logistics partner is compromised in its own estate and its over-privileged integration account is used to corrupt order data, stopping despatch.
consequences: Fulfilment disruption Nexora cannot fix directly
Contractual dispute during the outage

riskScenarios.title: Non-production environment as a route into production
riskScenarios.statement: A loosely controlled test environment is taken over and the legacy peering link carries the actor into the production tenancy.
consequences: Production compromise originating somewhere nobody watches

riskScenarios.title: Recovery fails when it is needed
riskScenarios.statement: Following any destructive incident, recovery does not complete within business tolerance because backups share administrative credentials with production and restores have never been timed.
consequences: Days rather than hours of outage
Extortion leverage is materially greater

riskScenarios.title: Material intrusion goes unnoticed
riskScenarios.statement: An intrusion progresses to business impact without detection, because the estate that matters most sends the least telemetry and escalation quality is poor.
consequences: Dwell time measured in months
Reconstruction impossible after the fact

riskScenarios.title: Cardholder data outside the regulated boundary
riskScenarios.statement: Card data present in application logs outside the defined payment environment creates regulatory exposure and widens what an actor can take from a routine compromise.
consequences: Acquirer and regulator involvement
Compliance programme reopened

riskScenarios.title: Acquisition integration imports unknown compromise
riskScenarios.statement: Kestrel Digital's estate is joined to the corporate network before anyone has examined it, importing whatever is already inside it.
consequences: A compromise Nexora inherits rather than suffers
Integration deadline pressure against security conditions

riskScenarios.title: Cyber capability collapses under load
riskScenarios.statement: Sustained overload and unfilled vacancies degrade detection, delivery and response quality to the point where the organisation's controls stop being operated properly.
consequences: Controls that exist on paper stop working in practice
Key people leave

riskScenarios.title: A destructive attack stops the warehouses
riskScenarios.statement: An actor with no interest in money gets in through the remote access appliance, reaches administrative control through the identity platform and the jump servers, and wipes the warehouse estate so that Nexora is seen to stop.
consequences: Despatch stopped at three distribution centres
No ransom to pay and so nothing to buy time with
Rebuilt, not restored, if the backups were reached too

riskScenarios.title: Payments diverted through a compromised account
riskScenarios.statement: A compromised finance mailbox, or staff passwords taken from a supplier's breach, are used to change where Nexora sends supplier payments or salaries.
consequences: Money paid to criminals, and recovered only if the bank is quick
Suppliers or staff unpaid while it is untangled
Questions from the auditors about payment controls

riskScenarios.title: The customer platform changed through its own release process
riskScenarios.statement: An engineer's machine is compromised, the build pipeline is used to ship the actor's code, and customers use a checkout Nexora did not write.
consequences: Card details taken at the checkout
Customers told to check their statements
The release process stopped while it is rebuilt

hypothesisTemplates.title: Supplier privileged access could enable major disruption
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Compromise of a third-party privileged identity could enable an actor to reach production administration and disrupt several critical business services.

hypothesisTemplates.title: One identity platform underpins several critical services
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Because staff, partner and service identities resolve to a single platform, its compromise would affect several critical business services simultaneously.

hypothesisTemplates.title: The legacy estate is not isolated from production
hypothesisTemplates.statement: An unsupported legacy estate, reachable from the corporate network and routable into production, could allow a routine compromise to become an operational outage.

hypothesisTemplates.title: Customer records are reachable from an internet-facing weakness
hypothesisTemplates.statement: An exploitable internet-facing service combined with over-permissioned workload identity could allow bulk extraction of customer records.

hypothesisTemplates.title: Partner identities start inside the staff boundary
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Because partner accounts share the staff directory, credential abuse against the extranet would begin from inside the internal identity boundary.

hypothesisTemplates.title: The deployment pipeline is a privileged path into production
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Standing production credentials in the build pipeline mean that compromise of an engineer or a repository becomes compromise of production.

hypothesisTemplates.title: Commercially sensitive data could be taken slowly
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Broad standing access to the behavioural data lake, with no egress monitoring, would allow patient extraction below any current detection threshold.

hypothesisTemplates.title: A supplier integration holds more authority than it needs
hypothesisTemplates.statement: An over-privileged integration account means a supplier's own compromise could stop Nexora's fulfilment.

hypothesisTemplates.title: Recovery would not complete within business tolerance
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Untested restores and backups sharing credentials with production mean that recovery from a destructive incident would take days rather than hours.

hypothesisTemplates.title: A material intrusion could progress unnoticed
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Telemetry gaps in the estate that matters most, combined with poor escalation quality, mean an intrusion could reach business impact without detection.

hypothesisTemplates.title: The regulated payment boundary is wider than documented
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Cardholder data outside the defined payment environment widens both regulatory exposure and what an ordinary compromise would yield.

hypothesisTemplates.title: The acquisition would import unexamined risk
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Connecting an estate nobody has examined to the corporate network would import whatever is already inside it.

hypothesisTemplates.title: Non-production is a route into production
hypothesisTemplates.statement: A peering link from a loosely controlled test environment into the production tenancy makes the weakest environment a path to the strongest.

hypothesisTemplates.title: The team cannot sustain the current load
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Sustained overload and unfilled vacancies would degrade the operation of controls that currently exist only because people compensate for them.

hypothesisTemplates.title: Somebody could stop the warehouses just to be seen to
hypothesisTemplates.statement: An actor that wants disruption rather than money could reach the warehouse estate from the edge of the network and destroy it, with no negotiation to slow them.

hypothesisTemplates.title: Supplier and salary payments can be redirected by email
hypothesisTemplates.statement: Whoever controls a finance mailbox, or a reused staff password, could change where Nexora's money goes without anyone checking by other means.

hypothesisTemplates.title: The release pipeline would ship an intruder's code
hypothesisTemplates.statement: The build pipeline deploys whatever reaches it, so anyone who reaches it can change what customers use.

assumptions.statement: Multi-factor authentication covers all external and administrative access.
The managed service provider holds no standing privileged access.
The legacy estate remains isolated from the production environment.
Backups recover critical services within business tolerance.
The legacy platform retires before the end of Q3.
The payment platform's exposure does not change materially this year.
Standing privileged exceptions remain at a manageable level.
There is no adversary currently operating inside the environment.
Monitoring coverage is sufficient to detect a material intrusion.
The cloud migration completes to its current schedule.

rationaleTags.label: Compensating controls are sufficient
rationaleTags.description: Other controls reduce this to a level the business can carry.

rationaleTags.label: Business disruption would be disproportionate
rationaleTags.description: The remedy costs the business more than the risk does.

rationaleTags.label: More evidence is required
rationaleTags.description: The picture is not yet good enough to act on.

rationaleTags.label: The system retires imminently
rationaleTags.description: The exposure ends with the system.

rationaleTags.label: Residual risk is within tolerance
rationaleTags.description: This sits inside what the organisation has said it will accept.

rationaleTags.label: This requires executive ownership
rationaleTags.description: The decision is not the CISO's to take alone.

rationaleTags.label: Resource constraints require deferral
rationaleTags.description: There is no capacity to do this properly right now.

rationaleTags.label: This enables a business objective
rationaleTags.description: The choice supports something the organisation is trying to achieve.

rationaleTags.label: The consequence is material
rationaleTags.description: If this happened, the business could not absorb it.

rationaleTags.label: The precedent matters
rationaleTags.description: How this is handled will shape what is asked for next.

rationaleTags.label: Regulatory exposure requires action
rationaleTags.description: There is an external obligation here, not only a risk judgement.

rationaleTags.label: The decision is reversible
rationaleTags.description: This can be revisited cheaply if the picture changes.
